name: local-missed-requirement
about: A local job whose earlier leads often missed a hard requirement or gave a wrong number.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Of 58 of our ad leads in the last 28 days, 44 were called and 25 were reached.
21 of 58 of our ad leads in the last 28 days did not meet a hard requirement of the opening.
9 of the 44 ad leads we called in the last 28 days had a wrong number.

output.audience: Class A drivers who already meet the years requirement the opening states, now on runs that keep them out overnight or over weekends. They stop for hourly pay and a home-daily, Monday to Friday week in a day cab, and they are willing to handle touch freight.

angles.idea: Lead with who qualifies: a Class A licence and the years requirement the opening states, said before any benefit.
angles.proof: The opening is a Class A job and states a years requirement.
angles.why: A large share of recent leads failed a hard requirement, so stating it up front is worth more than attraction. Office should confirm what the years figure covers.

angles.idea: Lead with the hourly pay rate for local work, with health insurance named beside it.
angles.proof: The opening states an hourly pay rate and offers health insurance.
angles.why: Hourly pay is the clearest term on the job for a local driver. No hook or scene has been measured yet, so this is untested.

angles.idea: Lead with the week: home daily on a Monday to Friday schedule, shown as the driver back on their own street.
angles.proof: The opening offers home daily and lists Monday to Friday.
angles.why: The schedule is what a driver on longer runs lacks. Nothing has been measured for this pairing, so treat it as a test.

angles.idea: Lead with the day cab running local delivery, a truck with no sleeper because the driver goes home daily.
angles.proof: The job is local delivery in a day cab and offers home daily.
angles.why: The day cab shows the home-daily claim without needing words. Untested here, since no earlier ad results exist by hook or scene.

angles.idea: Say plainly that this is touch freight: the driver handles the load, and the pay is by the hour.
angles.proof: The opening lists touch freight and pays an hourly rate.
angles.why: Drivers who will not handle freight should rule themselves out before the form. Thin link: the outcomes do not say which requirement leads failed.
